tier_reason: First-party Criterion benchmark (tomtomwombat/bench-bloom-filters, benches/bench_bloom_filter.rs) is public and the CPU (Ryzen 9 5900X) is stated, but no rustc version or flags are given, so it falls short of A and stays C.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README headline: "2-20 times faster and magnitudes more accurate than existing Bloom filter implementations". Per-check latency charts on the page: non-member check fastbloom 1.36 ns (atomic 1.61) vs sbbf 5.16, bloomfilter 14.50, bloom 17.44, probabilistic-collections 21.29, solana-bloom 42.56 ns (~3.8x-31x, derived from page data); member check fastbloom 7.67 ns (atomic 7.38) vs bloom 27.26, bloomfilter 29.45, probabilistic-collections 35.19, solana-bloom 121.56 ns (~3.6x-16x, derived from page data), but sbbf is faster on member checks at 5.30 ns (fastbloom ~1.45x slower, derived from page data).
corrections.workload: Per-lookup latency (ns) of member and non-member checks on u64 keys in a 64 KiB (2^16-byte) filter holding 45,000 items (~8 hashes/item), measured with Criterion against other Rust Bloom filter crates (sbbf-rs-safe, bloomfilter, bloom, probabilistic-collections, solana-bloom). fastbloom uses foldhash, the others SipHash-1-3 (xxhash for sbbf). No insert benchmark is charted.
corrections.caveats: The claim is overstated: on the page's own member-check chart sbbf (5.30 ns) beats fastbloom (7.67 ns), so "2-20x faster than existing implementations" does not hold for every crate or operation. fastbloom was benchmarked with foldhash while bloom, bloomfilter and probabilistic-collections used SipHash-1-3, so part of the gap is the hasher (fastbloom's own default is SipHash-1-3). The benchmark repo has no license, no rustc version or flags are stated, the numbers exist only as labels on chart images, and it measures lookups only, with no insert throughput.

notes: The record's claim quotes the README correctly but hides that sbbf wins member checks. The chart images do carry exact numeric labels, which are now quoted.
